endorsements.title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for AI-Enabled Device Software Functions (final guidance)
endorsements.quote: We strongly encourage manufacturers to consider discussing a proposed PCCP containing modifications that are implemented automatically with FDA through the Pre-Submission process prior to submitting a marketing submission to receive feedback on those modifications and the proposed PCCP.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: In situations where manufacturers wish to consider development of models that automatically or continuously update, FDA encourages manufacturers to use the Q-S ubmission Program to discuss considerations related to these AI models early in the development process and review the FDA guidance titled “Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions.”

commentary.bottom_line: Two FDA guidance documents encourage manufacturers to discuss proposed predetermined change control plans through the Pre-Submission (Q-Submission) process, especially for models that update automatically, but no study has tested whether early engagement improves plan adequacy or review outcomes. The recommendation rests on regulatory expectation rather than measured effect.

perspectives.view: No study in this map compares predetermined change control plans that went through a Pre-Submission with those that did not. No study documents how often regulators find plans inadequate. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence, and the endorsements count as expert and agency opinion.

The final PCCP guidance strongly encourages Pre-Submission discussion for plans containing automatically implemented modifications, and the draft lifecycle guidance encourages Q-Submission use early in development for continuously updating models. Both use should-level language, so the practice is voluntary, and neither document reports data on whether this engagement changes authorization outcomes or timelines.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare marketing submissions with and without prior Pre-Submission discussion of a change control plan, measuring additional-information requests, review time, authorization rates, and the scope of modifications FDA accepts. FDA or manufacturers could report aggregate data on how often proposed modification types are narrowed or rejected and whether early feedback reduces that rate.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested this practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Neither guidance excerpt addresses whether Pre-Submission discussions should examine how automatic modifications perform in these groups, which leaves any effect on them unknown.
